picks.title: Meditation: Resting in Reality (24 min)
picks.summary: In this guided meditation, Tara Brach invites us to relax out of the thinking mind and return to the living presence of the moment. Through a gentle body scan, awareness of breath, sound and sensation, we begin to sense the aliveness that is always here—and to rest more fully in reality. As the mind naturally wanders into thought, we practice letting go and opening again to the changing river of experience. Whatever arises—ease or discomfort, sorrow, fear or peace—can be met with kindness and allowed to belong. This meditation offers a pathway to embodied presence, inner stillness and the natu
picks.reason: A guided meditation inviting presence and kindness with all experience, central to Buddhist practice.

picks.title: Renate Seifarth: Ursachen von dukkha
picks.summary: (Buddha-Haus) Die Ursachen von Leiden, dukkha, sind manigfach. Zum einen werden Formen des Verlangens und des Ablehnens, die Triebe, die Ausflüsse - asavas - genannt. Zum anderen die Unwissenheit, die Täuschung über das Wesen aller Personen und Erscheinungen. Unsere falschen Annahmen und unser greifendes Verhalten führt zu Verstrickung und Leid. Unsere Aufgabe besteht darin, die Täuschung zu durchschauen und unsere Triebe lenken zu können oder loslassen zu können.
picks.reason: A detailed talk on the Buddhist causes of suffering and how to overcome craving and ignorance.

picks.title: From Uganda to the Dalai Lama: The Chronicles of an African Seeker in India | Bhante Buddharakkhita
picks.summary:
In this talk, Bhante Buddharakkhita, visiting from Uganda, speaks about his journey from Africa  into Buddhism, and how the first four blessings described by the Buddha in the Maṇgala Sutta (Discourse on Blessings - https://www.dhammatalks.org/books/ChantingGuide/Section0051.html) can help keep us on the path. Learn more at https://bhantebuddharakkhita.org/ and https://ugandabuddhistcenter.org/



Bio

Bhante first encountered Buddhism in 1990 while studying and living in India. He was ordained as a Buddhist monk by the late Most Venerable U Silananda in 2002 at the Tathagata Meditation Center
picks.reason: A personal journey into Buddhism with reflections on the Mangala Sutta's blessings.

picks.reason: A Buddhist monk discusses the question of life's purpose and overcoming purposelessness.

picks.title: Connecting with our Inner Buddha | Venerable Hue Can  | 4 September 2026
picks.summary: Venerable Hue Can is the Abbess of Sunyata Meditation Centre in Vic Park and has the very clear goal to teach others how to realize their full potential through Zen Buddhism. Venerable Hue Can had an interesting and diverse career as a teacher, Children’s Librarian and co-ordinator of the Ethnic Child Care Resource Unit. As an advocate for access and equity she have worked in the area of social welfare, particularly in the Vietnamese community in Western Australia. When the Most Venerable Master Thich Thanh Tu came to Perth in 1996 she was fortunate to attend his lecture “Why am I a Buddhist”.
picks.reason: A Zen Buddhist abbess teaches realizing potential through Zen practice and social engagement.

picks.title: Renate Seifarth: Liebe als Antwort auf Leiden
picks.summary: (Buddha-Haus) Dukkha ist Teil der Welt. Es braucht eine Antwort darauf. Weisheit bringt uns Gelassenheit, Liebe - metta - und Mitgefühl - karuna - spenden Trost. Weisheit und Metta gehören wie zwei Seiten einer Münzen untrennbar zu unserer Praxis der inneren Befreiung. Lieben wird gehindert durch Erwartungen. Weisheit befreit uns von solchen.
picks.reason: A talk on love, wisdom, and compassion as responses to suffering in Buddhist practice.

picks.title: The True Nature of Devotion In Our Lives
picks.summary: In this talk Samantabhadri explores what it was like to meet the Buddha, the fully Enlightened human being. She then discusses 'garava' as devotion for the whole richness of our Dharma Lives, including positive emotions for all beings. This talk was given on an Order weekend at  Taraloka Retreat Centre, 2022.  ***  Help us keep FBA Podcasts free for everyone! picks.reason: Explores devotion in Buddhist life, including positive emotions and meeting the Buddha.

picks.title: Pathways to Trusting the Gold
picks.summary: What would it mean to truly trust the goodness that lives within you? In this talk, Tara Brach explores what she calls "trusting the gold"—awakening from the stories of deficiency, fear and separation that keep us from recognizing our deepest nature. We may spend much of our lives trying to improve ourselves, earn approval or finally become "enough," while overlooking the loving awareness that is already here. Tara explores how our early experiences of nurturing and belonging shape our capacity to trust ourselves, and how mindfulness and compassion can help heal the places that feel unworthy,
picks.reason: Tara Brach explores trusting our innate goodness from a Buddhist-inspired view.

picks.reason: Zen teacher reflects on accountability and letting go of greed with a classic Zen story.
